title: Complexity Bounds for Dirichlet Process Slice Samplers
topic: Probabilistic Methods->Monte Carlo and Sampling Methods
claim: Sampling from a discrete random measure is equivalent to drawing a slice level, then picking uniformly among atoms above it.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, formula atop each, shared bar/step visuals
description: Three side-by-side panels with axes, each headed by a formula in large math type. Left: red bars of varying heights labeled π1, π2, π3, π4, …, πk above atoms φ1, φ2, …, φk on an x-axis, showing the discrete measure G(dx)=Σ πk δφk. Center: a blue decreasing step function of u, with solid steps and a dashed continuation toward the left, labeled with sorted weights πk, π4, π2, π3, π1 on the x-axis and counts 1–5 on the y-axis, matching p(u)=Σ 1(0<u<πk). Right: the bar chart again, with a horizontal dashed blue line at u=u0. The portions of bars above the line are red, and the parts below are gray. Bars above the line, φ1 and φ3, are highlighted in bold. Text at top reads 'Sample u0 ~ p(u), then x ~ Uniform({φk : πk > u0})'. The eye goes first to the red bars, then to the blue staircase.
caption: Distributions involved in the slice sampler. Sampling $x\sim G(dx)$ is equivalent to sampling $u\sim p(u)$ and $x\mid u \sim p(x\mid u)$. Left panel: A realization of a discrete probability measure $G(\mathrm{d}x) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \pi_k \delta_{\phi_k}(\mathrm{d}x)$, represented as point masses located at atoms $\phi_k$ with weights $\pi_k$. Sampling $x \sim G$ corresponds to selecting one atom $\phi_k$ with probability $\pi_k$. Center panel: The marginal distribution of the auxiliary slice variable $u$, given by $p(u) = \sum_{k\ge1} \mathbbm{1}(0<u<\pi_k)$, which is a decreasing step function supported on $(0, \max_k \pi_k)$. Right panel: Slice-sampling mechanism. First, a slice value $u_0$ is drawn from $p(u)$ (horizontal dashed line). Conditionally on $u_0$, the variable $x$ is sampled uniformly from the finite set $\{\phi_k : \pi_k > u_0\}$, corresponding to atoms whose weights exceed the slice level.
abstract: Slice sampling is a standard Monte Carlo technique for Dirichlet process (DP)-based models, widely used in posterior simulation. However, formal assessments of the scalability of posterior slice samplers have remained largely unexplored, primarily because the computational cost of a slice-sampling iteration is random and potentially unbounded. In this work, we obtain high-probability bounds on the computational complexity of DP slice samplers. Our main results show that, uniformly across posterior cluster-growth regimes, the overhead induced by slice variables, relatively to the number of clusters supported by the posterior, is $O_{\mathbb P}(\log n)$. As a consequence, even in worst-case configurations, superlinear blow-ups in per-iteration computational cost occur with vanishing probability. Our analysis applies broadly to DP-based models without any likelihood-specific assumptions, still providing complexity guarantees for posterior sampling on arbitrary datasets. These results establish a theoretical foundation for assessing the practical scalability of slice sampling in DP-based models.
